headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared-bus Pipecat interacting with OpenBB MCP/IO surfaces; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP and API surfaces, while pipecat has a shared-bus concurrency model and multiple transport/input channels. That creates a plausible path for Pipecat-delivered content to reach OpenBB as trusted instructions, even though no direct bridge is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards user or remote content into an MCP-connected OpenBB session without provenance tagging, injection is plausible.
IF OpenBB parses file or MCP content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable any MCP bridge between the agents.
Require provenance labels on all Pipecat-fed text before OpenBB consumes it.
Use a manual approval step for any OpenBB tool invocation triggered by Pipecat.
Run the agents in separate OS users or containers.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBB touches financial, licensed, and public data, but its profile shows no filesystem read/write or network egress. Pipecat has allowlisted egress and handles text, audio, video, and conversation state, yet no shared workspace or authenticated principal is shown. The pair can leak data only through an unusual integration path, so low fits.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same workspace or message bus, sensitive OpenBB outputs can reach Pipecat.
IF Pipecat is configured to send conversation state containing OpenBB outputs to third-party STT/LLM/TTS services, leakage expands.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pass OpenBB outputs into Pipecat conversation state.
Review Pipecat service endpoints and disable unused third-party providers.
Use local-only transports where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBB cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while Pipecat’s profile shows no write or git capability. Both support multiple instances, but the documented surfaces do not show overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflicts become possible.
IF Pipecat is extended with a writable plugin or shared database, contention can emerge.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources single-writer.
Avoid sharing git repositories between the agents.
Serialize any writes through one coordinator.
Audit orchestrator permissions before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat commonly routes text through LLM, STT, and TTS services, so it can treat upstream content as operational input. OpenBB can emit financial analysis that Pipecat may relay or act on, creating a plausible chain where unverified OpenBB output becomes downstream action or speech. No verification step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses OpenBB output as authoritative text for speech, routing, or agent actions, errors can cascade.
IF OpenBB outputs stale or incorrect financial facts and Pipecat forwards them without verification, downstream harm increases.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pipecat consumes OpenBB output.
Mark OpenBB output as advisory, not authoritative.
Require human review for any action derived from financial facts.
Log source provenance alongside every forwarded claim.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against primary market data.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBB explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while Pipecat’s documented services include third-party STT/LLM/TTS and analytics endpoints with allowlisted egress. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated or licensed data flows into Pipecat providers, even though residency and certification details are not documented. Uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data from OpenBB is sent through Pipecat to third-party providers, policy obligations may be triggered.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not provided by the chosen Pipecat services, compliance gaps appear.
mitigations: Restrict Pipecat to approved providers only.
Do not route licensed or regulated OpenBB data through external STT/LLM/TTS services.
Review retention settings for every enabled Pipecat endpoint.
Document the data flow for compliance review.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls.
